rules: This file is the only place a value is typed by hand; src/ward.css and src/tokens.ts are generated from it.
Dark value in brackets in the review where it differs; here dark lives beside light under 'dark' / 'chipDark'.
Closed unions (chip roles, marker kinds/sizes, stream steps, live event types) are generated from this file; extending one is a tokens.json change first.

Dark stream chip pairs for steps 1–3 derived by the deep-tint rule (deep hue tint + light hue text) and measured: s1 #45C4B4 on #0E2622 7.44:1, s2 #C0A2F0 on #1D1533 8.01:1, s3 #F0A46B on #27160A 8.48:1 — all ≥ 4.5:1.
live.staleAfter = live.staleAfterPolls × live.poll (3 × 15s = 45s).

pad/gap and the colHead..handleMark type tokens are transcribed verbatim from design/*.dc.html, reading only .app subtrees — the .dv-* classes in those files are design-viewer chrome (#1a1a1a, #e9e8e4, 4px radii, 40px 44px 32px page padding) and are NOT Trellis.

The comps specify light theme only: none of the six declares data-theme, and #7FB2FF/#8FA3C8/#7FD3A0/#E7C57F are console syntax colours on the #0B1631 console block, not a dark ramp. Dark values for line3/ink2/surface3 are DERIVED BY ANALOGY to the existing dark ramp and are not measured from any design source.

consoleInfo/consoleOk/consoleWarn/consoleDim ARE measured: they are the four .cl colours on the .cons block in Trellis Board Item.dc.html (#7FB2FF info, #7FD3A0 ok, #E7C57F warn, #8FA3C8 dim). They carry the same value in light and dark because the console surface is #0B1631 in both themes, so no dark twin has to be invented. check.mjs measures all four against color.console (7.02-10.82:1).

breakpoint.railStack (792) and breakpoint.singleColumn (476) are DERIVED, not measured: no comp declares a single @media query and all six are a fixed 1240px canvas, so the design source says nothing about reflow. They are arithmetic on measured widths rather than chosen round numbers — 792 = width.sidebar 236 + width.colFloor 240 + width.rail 316, the width below which three columns cannot coexist without the centre falling under its floor; 476 = width.sidebar 236 + width.colFloor 240, where two cannot. A @media condition cannot read a CSS custom property, so these values appear literally in component CSS as (breakpoint - 0.02) and the 'one breakpoint scale' gate enforces that correspondence.

color.greenFill (#00897B) and color.orangeFill (#BF5310) are the comp's SOLID-FILL hues, distinct from the ink hues color.green (#0C7A4D) and color.orange (#B14E12). They are measured: every one of the 21 #00897B uses and every #BF5310 dot across design/*.dc.html is a background on a sized element, never text. greenFill is 4.32:1 on white and so is DECORATION-ONLY like color.faint — it must never carry content; orangeFill is 4.71:1 and does pass AA. Their dark twins are NOT invented: dark.orangeFill #F0A46B is the value already derived and measured for dark.orange and stream s3, and dark.greenFill #45C4B4 is stream s1's derived twin, reused because #00897B is two points off s1's #00776B. Both remain design-unsourced in the sense that rule 8 means — the comps are light-theme only.

breakpoint.medium (1024) and breakpoint.small (768) are neither measured nor derived: they are the conventional tablet widths the pre-scale code already used, and they are declared here rather than re-derived because each is tuned to one component's own content, which the shell's widths are not. railStack and singleColumn answer 'which columns can exist'; medium and small answer 'does this component's content still fit in a row' — different questions, so one scale for both would be wrong. Forcing TopBar's list-to-select swap from 768 down to 476 would leave a full nav list in a 392px centre column, and the same applies to PageHeader stacking. They are named by position in the scale rather than by device because each serves two unrelated purposes: 1024 drops a table's second column tier AND widens Overlay's drawer to full width; 768 stacks PageHeader AND makes that drawer full-height. The real defect they fix is that the same intent was spelled two ways — 1024 and 1023.98, 768 and 767.98 — so a table and a drawer disagreed by one pixel about where the same breakpoint was. The 'one breakpoint scale' gate now requires the (breakpoint - 0.02) form and a declared token, so that cannot recur. Both remain candidates for replacement by container queries, which is the architecturally correct answer: these components sit in variable-width columns, so a table in the 316px rail currently believes it is on a 2560px screen.

width.maxWide (1928) is DERIVED for the same reason breakpoint.* is: the comps are a fixed 1240px canvas and say nothing about screens larger than themselves. It is arithmetic on measured widths, and the two readings agree: width.max 1240 + the comp's own centre column (1240 - sidebar 236 - rail 316 = 688) = 1928, which is also sidebar + 2x688 + rail. So it is the widest the shell can be while the centre column stays within TWICE its mirrored measure — the only statement the comps make about how wide that column should be. The flanking columns do NOT grow with it: 236 and 316 are measured, and widening them is unsourced invention. Note that a 27-inch 4K panel at macOS default scaling presents ~1920 CSS px, which fills 1928 to within 8px, so the common large-desktop case gets the whole canvas and only genuinely wider viewports (2560 native) letterbox.

width.rail (316), height.app (760) and type.microHead ARE measured, from the .app rule in design/Trellis Studio.dc.html (display:grid; grid-template-columns:236px 1fr 316px; min-height:760px) and the .k rule in design/Trellis Platform Surface.dc.html (500 9px/1 mono, .13em, uppercase). width.rail duplicates width.dryrun's value on purpose: 316 is the shell's third column, and DryRunRail is only one thing that can occupy it, so AppShell must not depend on a token named for an occupant. type.microHead is the same measurement as .th in Trellis Admin.dc.html, so the admin table-head work should reuse it rather than add a second name.

containerBreakpoint.wide (688) and .narrow (472) are DERIVED, and they are a SECOND scale rather than an extension of breakpoint.*: a viewport width and a column width are different quantities. Each is the centre column's width at the viewport width where Grid's existing data-drop tiers already fire — 688 = breakpoint.canvas 1240 - width.sidebar 236 - width.rail 316, and 472 = breakpoint.medium 1024 - 236 - 316. Moving those tiers from @media to @container therefore preserves the current behaviour exactly at the shell's canonical widths, while making them ALSO fire when a column rather than a window is what squeezes them — the defect named in the breakpoint.medium rule above, where a table in the 316px rail believes it is on a 2560px screen. Note 472 is not breakpoint.singleColumn 476: 476 is width.sidebar + width.colFloor, the VIEWPORT width at which the centre hits its floor, which is a different measurement that happens to land four pixels away. Containment is ignored on internal table elements, so a <tr> cannot be the container and the query must name an ancestor the component does not own; Grid establishes one on a wrapper around its <table>.

Sidebar (Q18) tokens are all MEASURED from the first .col of .app in design/Trellis Studio.dc.html, and most of what it needs already existed. Only three type tokens are new: type.brandMark (named 600 13/1, -.01em) exists separately from type.cardTitle, which is the same font at the same size WITHOUT tracking and is already used elsewhere — adding tracking to cardTitle would silently change every existing user, and the comp's brand row does declare letter-spacing:-.01em. type.navAction (prose 600 11/1, the blue 'New') and type.agentActive (prose 600 12.5/1, the selected agent's name) had no match. Everything else is reuse: the nav item is type.tabLabel, the agent name type.rowName, its meta type.rowNote, the footer link type.ruleCond, and the group head the measured type.microHead. The pad.sidebar* and gap.sidebar* values are named single-purpose tokens for the same reason pad.configRow and gap.band are: 13, 14, 9, 11, 10, 5 and 7 are NOT on Ward's 4px space scale, because the comps are not on a 4px scale, and quantising them to it is the re-quantisation that gate 3b exists to stop. height.brandMark 15 and height.agentDot 7 follow the existing height.traceDot 6 precedent and are used for both dimensions since both marks are squares. IMPORTANT, and it corrects an earlier claim of mine recorded in TODO Q18: the agent dots are NOT an inconsistent decorative palette and they do NOT need a new colour token. The four filled dots are #00897B, #00897B, #7038C8, #BF5310, which are exactly stream.s1.id, s1, s2 and s3 — so the dot is the agent's STREAM IDENTITY, already generated as --ward-stream-<n>-id. It read as inconsistent only because two of the agents are on the same stream, one draft and one live, which is what you would see precisely IF the hue tracked stream rather than state. So Sidebar takes streamStep per agent, the same way Chip and StreamRow already do. The one thing the comp does encode as state is paused: a hollow dot (box-shadow inset 0 0 0 1px, no background) with the name in color.muted.

WorkCard (Q20, no comp) once forced an exact JS-computed height on every card (height.card + space.4 x fields-rows) to stop titles and meta text wrapping arbitrarily and producing different heights for no real reason. That formula went through two miscalibrations — once undershooting so the last line clipped off the bottom, once overshooting so a one-line title carried a full blank reserved line under it — before the real fix: title and the meta 'waits on X' text are single-line + ellipsis now, the same truncation idiom .mono/.field/.last/BoardColumn's .label already use, so they cannot wrap and cause variance in the first place. With every text line and the fields-row count already deterministic per board, the JS height formula became dead weight and was removed; natural CSS sizing now gives every card on a board the same height on its own. The one line that still varies on purpose is the last-agent-action/finding note: it renders nothing at all (Last returns null, mirroring Fields' existing null-when-empty pattern) rather than an empty reserved line when an item has neither, so a card with that data is slightly taller than one without — an honest difference in what the item has, not an accident of title length.
pad.pageHeader (18px 20px 14px) is MEASURED from the Admin comp page head: <div class="row" style="padding:18px 20px 14px;align-items:flex-start">.

Dark chip.quiet reuses soft's ground with dark muted ink.

Label-to-control (gap.formLabel 6) and the footer gap (gap.modalFooter 8) already existed.
